assets.statement: regular n-gon is a valid witness (every centre, every radius r>0 hits ≤2 other vertices; machine-checked n∈[3,64], hand-checked n=3,4,5) determining exactly ⌊n/2⌋ < (1+c)n/2 distinct distances for every c>0, all n≥3 — literal negation of the canonical claim; imported from erdos653-campaign-001 R007/

A=ℝ satisfies the frozen premise (infinite subset of ℝ) but defeats the conclusion, since every affine image aA+b is all of ℝ and no proper E contains it; the canonical universal statement is false as written and requires an added smallness hypothesis on A.

explicit 4-periodic walk over S={e1,e2} satisfies all frozen premises yet its four-point image (unit square vertices) has no three collinear points; canonical statement is false as frozen and must be re-frozen with an injectivity/unboundedness premise before either branch can close nontrivially

Zero-step degenerate walk (S∋0, constant walk, singleton A) satisfies all stated premises and violates the conclusion; statement needs 0∉S and infinitely many distinct points before the real conjecture is engaged.

The Bool-valued check is a closed-form certificate generator: `multiplicity n d ≤ 2` on every chord-distance class d ∈ [1, ⌊n/2⌋] certifies the premise for EVERY centre x_i and EVERY radius r > 0 (each vertex-to-vertex distance is realized by at most 2 other vertices, so no circle centred at a vertex contains 3 other points — the contract's problem-specific trap is discharged by the all-radii argument, not by checking special radii); `(List.range (n/2)).length = ⌊n/2⌋` is the exact distinct-distance count D = ⌊n/2⌋; and `2·⌊n/2⌋ ≤ n < (1+c)·n` for every real c > 0 gives the strict violation D

Regular n-gon is a counterexample: d(k)^2=4sin^2(pi k/n) gives at most 2 vertices on every circle centred at any vertex with any radius r>0 (premise holds, machine-checked n in [3,360] fail-closed), and exactly floor(n/2) distinct distances, which is less than (1+c)n/2 for every c>0 and all n>=3.
